source_span: The upward revision to the longer-run neutral rate to 3.25%, in our view, strengthens the case for a higher terminal policy rate (two additional 25bp hikes rather than one).
source_chain: Warsh calls the hike 'removing a dose of accommodation' and says policy is not yet restrictive, and the committee revises its neutral-rate estimate up to 3.25% from 3.06%, therefore any given policy rate delivers less restraint than previously assumed, therefore MS raises its call to two more hikes (December, March) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal — unless the Middle East conflict de-escalates or disinflation runs faster than expected, in which case December is the last hike and the March hike does not happen.
pulse_chain: The Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, Warsh calls it removing accommodation and says policy is still not restrictive, and the committee's neutral-rate estimate rises to 3.25% from 3.06%, therefore any given rate slows the economy less than the Fed assumed in June, therefore Morgan Stanley calls for two more hikes (December, March) to 4.25-4.50% against the market's four priced — unless a faster Middle East de-escalation or quicker disinflation makes December the last hike instead of the first of several.
why: The pulse reproduces MS's exact inferential step (higher neutral rate -> less restraint at any given rate -> two more hikes to 4.25-4.50%) and its stated invalidation (Middle East de-escalation/faster disinflation caps it at one more hike), and the secondary Goldman split (underdelivers-to-two house view; October hike added but 3.25-3.50% terminal held via 2027 cuts) checks out verbatim against the GS Pasquariello and GS Coppersmith notes with correct attribution.
